title: TON oscillator and output feedback
summary: Build a 500 ms TON blinker in Structured Text and check its on and off times with FOR and AT assertions.
scope: Tests provide native POSIX host evidence only; they are not physical LED, hardware timing, HIL, or certification evidence.
objectives: Build a {{t:500}} ms oscillator from a TON timer and output feedback.
Check its on and off times with FOR and AT assertions.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/Blinky.st, build the oscillator around one TON with PT T#500ms, for example BlinkTimer: keep it running with IN := TRUE, and when its Q is TRUE flip a state variable such as LedState and restart the timer with one call using IN := FALSE; LED_Output follows the state.
stages.checkpoint: The timer's output feeds back to flip the state and restart the timer, and the LED starts OFF.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, predict LED_Output at {{t:250}}, {{t:750}}, {{t:1250}}, and {{t:1750}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: OFF at {{t:250}} ms, ON at {{t:750}}, OFF at {{t:1250}}, ON at {{t:1750}}; the first rising edge lands between {{t:400}} and {{t:600}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then run: The starter holds LED_Output OFF forever; add a TON timer (T#500ms) that flips a state each time it expires, so the LED is OFF for about {{t:500}} ms, then ON for about {{t:500}} ms, repeating.
stages.checkpoint: The visible scenario must pass with saved host evidence.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: In Tests, choose the saved zplc.json and run only the BlinkyVisual scenario.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named BlinkyVisual and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Review the trace and table: OFF until about {{t:500}} ms, ON until about {{t:1000}} ms, OFF again, then ON from about {{t:1500}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: The three FOR windows ({{t:20}}-{{t:400}} ms OFF, {{t:620}}-{{t:900}} ms ON, {{t:1120}}-{{t:1400}} ms OFF) hold, and both rising edges and the falling edge are found.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: A program that toggles on every scan, blinks twice as fast, or stays ON only 20% of the time fails the FOR and AT assertions.
stages.checkpoint: The host scenario grades the logical waveform, not the technique (a {{t:500}} ms or {{t:510}} ms half period passes); it does not establish electrical period, brightness, hardware timing, HIL, or certification.

hints.text: A TON only finishes after its input has been TRUE for the whole preset, so the oscillator needs a timer whose output flips a state and then restarts the timer.
Declare a TON with PT T#500ms and a state variable; when the timer's Q is TRUE, invert the state and call the timer again with IN := FALSE so it restarts, and let LED_Output follow the state.

faultCases: The starter holds LED_Output OFF forever; add a TON timer (T#500ms) that flips a state each time it expires, so the LED is OFF for about 500 ms, then ON for about 500 ms, repeating.
